doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Rollins's repertoire and the audition at Fantasy
summary: Rollins knew many tunes in several keys; Soskin's midnight audition at Fantasy with only Orrin and Sonny got him the gig alongside Tony Williams and Donald Byrd.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: So in order for them to make a good showing do you tell them you’d better know this list of tunes?

Yes. Well repertoire is definitely important. So I mean look, Sonny knew so many tunes, you know ridiculous. He knew so many tunes, not only knew the tunes but knew them in several keys. So I would tell people learn the tunes and learn them in several different keys. And that’s very important to do.
Have you ever had a student go to one of those things and come in the next day and say oh, I really blew it?

That can happen. That can definitely happen. I mean look, when I first got the call to do Sonny’s, come down to Fantasy Records and do this audition. An “audition” it was called. When I got to the studio, at 12 midnight, there was nobody there except Orrin and Sonny. That’s it. What am I going to do? I have to play? You know this is like I could get the gig. So you know you really have to just make the most of it. You know and I knew at the time that this was a big thing. And so when I went to do the audition I didn’t know every tune that Sonny called, but I knew a lot of them. I knew enough of them to get me the gig. And right after I auditioned Sonny goes, “Okay, you got the gig and we’re going to rehearse in a day or so” and that’s that. So right away I was thrown into Tony Williams on one side and Sonny Rollins on the other, and throw in Donald Byrd in there. And so I © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
had to be ready for this. I mean I was a lot younger then you know, and I really had to take care of business immediately.
